analysis.title: "As Challenging As We Have Seen": Goldman's Panic Index Hits Record 9.8 After Fifth-Biggest VIX Spike On Record... Here's What Happened After The Other Four
key_insights: Goldman's US Vol Panic Index hit a record 9.8 out of 10 after the S&P 500 fell seven straight sessions and the VIX jumped more than 16 points, the fifth-largest weekly VIX spike on record. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief.

S&P closed Friday at 6,910, down 8.6% on the week and up 0.9% YTD. Nasdaq 100 lost 10.4%, its worst week since March 2020, and is more than 20% below its Oct 6 high. SOX fell 17% and is down 33% since the start of October.
Cross-asset liquidation: gold -9.5%, bitcoin -14.2%, copper more than -9% on the week. Only Treasuries worked, with the 10Y yield down 19bps to 4.94%.

Thematic baskets were crushed: Drones -24.8%, Bitcoin Sensitive -24.0%, Quantum Computing -23.4%, NeoClouds -22.6%, Space & Satellites -19.9%. The best basket, Bond Proxies, lost 1.9%, which indicates liquidation.

After the four larger VIX spikes (Oct 2008, May 2010, Feb 2020, Apr 2025), the S&P averaged +5.1% next day, +3.3% one week later (up every time), -2.8% two weeks later, -0.7% one month later, and +26.5% one year later. Sample is only four.

Goldman's conclusion is that technicals point to a near-term bounce, but the market keeps struggling until there is more clarity on the Fed's path and the AI trade. Tyler Durden notes all four prior spikes ended with a policy rescue, while the Fed is still hiking.
Liquidity is poor. ETFs were over 39% of the tape on Friday and S&P top-of-book liquidity was $4MM, near the YTD low. Moves were larger than flows.
Dealers are short gamma, and were the most short gamma since 2019 earlier in the week. This is expected to let big moves feed on themselves.

CTAs are estimated net short $19BN of US equities after selling $57BN in a month, and are modeled as sellers in every scenario next week. S&P trigger levels are 7,596, 7,540 and 7,119, and the index at 6,910 is below all of them.

Funding cracked: the December S&P total return future fell from about FF+35 to about FF+20 into Friday's close after hedge funds covered about $25BN of futures shorts. Year-end funding is still at FF+100, and the premium could fade further if the drawdown continues.
Nasdaq 100 is technically oversold with a 14-day RSI of 26.5. The desk thinks systematic selling in Nasdaq futures is closer to its end than its start.

Copper fell more than 9% on tighter financial conditions and data center weakness, triggering CTA selling. Physical users were unable to absorb it because their gross longs were near multi-year highs, about 20% of open interest versus roughly double the norm, possibly front-running a US copper tariff.

GS TMT specialist Peter Callahan says tech is oversold with valuations at 10-year lows (Nasdaq 100 17x forward earnings, semis 12-13x). Investors are on a buyers' strike because no one can name a catalyst. Charts show names that have cut guidance (FFIV, INTC) outperforming, while companies and investors do not expect cuts.
Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all published 2027 S&P targets of 8,700 in the past two weeks, which is a 26% rally from Friday's close. Durden expects revisions within 4-6 weeks.

Sector color: industrials and materials lost about 7% each, levered small and mid caps were hit hard (TROX -42%, FMC -22%), and data center names fell (MTZ -20%, VRT -18%). Health care had a policy scare from the CRUSH/RADV proposal and Medicare-for-All headlines. Energy is cautious with Brent down 15% in a month and refiners the most shorted corner.
The coming week has a Thursday market holiday and a Friday half day. Options price a 3.27% S&P move through Nov 27. Durden's take is to rent the one-week bounce and respect the two-week trapdoor.

Vertiv fell 18% in the data center weakness selloff.
Tronox fell 42% on balance sheet and earnings worries in levered small and mid caps.
FMC fell 22% on the week amid levered small and mid cap weakness.

Intel has already cut and is starting to outperform, which the note reads as what the market wants to hear.

Each lost about 7% on the week, with levered small and mid caps hit on balance sheet and earnings worries.

earnings_insights: Keysight, Nvidia and Palo Alto reported beat-and-raise quarters last week, per Callahan, but the stocks did not hold up.

Upcoming Tuesday night tech earnings: Dell, Workday and HP, with Analog Devices, Autodesk, Nutanix, Zoom, HPE and Semtech also on the docket. Tuesday consumer earnings include Best Buy, Dick's, Burlington, Dollar Tree, Abercrombie and Urban Outfitters. Deere reports earnings and guidance. No EPS figures are given.

trade_ideas.description: Rent the near-term S&P bounce after the VIX spike and respect the two-week downside trapdoor
trade_ideas.rationale: After four prior VIX spikes larger than this one, the S&P was higher one week later every time and lower two weeks later three times out of four.
trade_ideas.risk: No policy rescue is likely while the Fed is hiking, and CTA supply and dealer short gamma could extend the drawdown.

risk_factors: Dealer short gamma and thin liquidity could amplify moves.
CTA selling is modeled in every scenario next week.
The Fed is still hiking with no policy rescue as in prior VIX spike episodes.
An AI trade unwind and possible estimate or capex cuts.
Funding premium fading if the drawdown continues.
A repeat of the 2018 Nasdaq 100 path.
charts_described: Chart of every weekly VIX change since 1990 shows only four weeks bigger than this one: Oct 10, 2008, May 7, 2010, Feb 28, 2020 and Apr 4, 2025.
Table of S&P performance after the four prior VIX spikes shows next-day average +5.1%, one-week +3.3%, two-week -2.8%, one-month -0.7%, one-year +26.5%.
Chart of the Nasdaq 100 from Nov 2017 through Dec 2018 against the past twelve months is the 2018 analog passed around by desks.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman US Vol Panic Index at a record 9.8 out of 10. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief.
VIX above 35 (closed above 37), term structure steeply inverted, skew very steep.
Weekly VIX change was the fifth-largest since 1990, behind the weeks ending Oct 10, 2008, May 7, 2010, Feb 28, 2020 and Apr 4, 2025.
Dealers are short gamma, the most short since 2019 as of Tuesday.
CTAs are net short $19BN of US equities after selling $57BN in a month. They are modeled as sellers in all scenarios over the next week, with S&P triggers at 7,596, 7,540 and 7,119.
Positioning is described as washed out and sentiment on the lows, but the non-systematic crowd has not sold much.
ETFs were over 39% of the tape Friday and S&P top-of-book liquidity was $4MM.
Options price a 3.27% S&P move through Nov 27.
Hedge funds covered about $25BN of futures shorts, and the Dec S&P TR future fell from about FF+35 to about FF+20.
Refiners are the most shorted corner of energy, and US natural gas is one of the better-owned hiding spots.
geopolitical: An FT report said hawkish officials in Washington and Israel are urging Trump to restart strikes on Iran, landing late Friday on a fragile tape.
Continued overseas tensions are cited by the derivatives desk as one of the pressures on the market.
A US copper tariff has yet to show up, and Goldman suspects physical users front-ran it.
cross_bank_references: Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all published S&P targets of 8,700 for 2027 within the past two weeks.
Durden's companion piece covers JPMorgan's and Goldman's positioning data.

tension_points.bull_case: After four larger VIX spikes the S&P was higher one week later every time, the Panic Index is above 9.5, the Nasdaq is oversold and systematic selling is near its end.
tension_points.bear_case: Two weeks later the S&P was lower three times out of four. CTAs are sellers in every scenario, dealers are short gamma, liquidity is thin, and the Fed is still hiking with no rescue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further drawdown toward 20% from the highs and continued CTA selling below the 7,119 long-term trigger would negate the bounce view.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals look firm, with beat-and-raise quarters from Keysight, Nvidia and Palo Alto, firm compute pricing, and valuations at 10-year lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Charts suggest guidance or estimate cuts are coming, since names that have cut (FFIV, INTC) are outperforming, and investors see no catalyst.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clear catalyst that turns sentiment, or actual estimate and capex cuts confirming the charts.
